bullets.title: Global bond rout deepens: US 10yr hits 4.75%, 30yr at 5.33% (2007 high)
bullets.body: US 10-year Treasury yields rose to 4.75% (highest since Jan 2025) while the 30-year hit 5.33%, the highest since 2007. The selloff is global — Germany's 30-year bond priced at its highest yield since 2011, Japan's 10-year hit a 3-decade peak, and the US yield curve steepened to a new cycle high (~50-55bps 10s2s). Drivers cited include AI-IG issuance crowding (+0.3ppts estimated on 10Y), fiscal deficit running +15% YoY to $1.17T, geopolitical risk, and Quad 3 inflation re-acceleration — with bond yields failing to respond to benign CPI/PPI (a bearish technical signal).

bullets.title: Iran-Hormuz tensions: Brent above $91, supertanker rates near $510k/day
bullets.body: Iran's top negotiator declared the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US meets interim deal conditions, while Trump claimed Hormuz as 'new American territory.' Brent crude pushed above $91 and oil supertanker rates soared toward $510,000/day. Hedgeye flagged WTI breaking above $83 as triggering inflation re-acceleration and a Quad 3 regime shift from disinflationary Quad 4, with next CPI expected to surprise to the upside.

bullets.title: BofA FMS: Fund managers at extreme bullish equity positioning; AI bubble top tail risk
bullets.body: BofA's August Fund Manager Survey shows net 56% of managers overweight equities (highest since Nov 2021) with cash at 3.5%, while net 27% are overweight US stocks (highest since Dec 2024). Concurrently, 32% cite an AI bubble as the top tail risk, and 49% expect stagflation over the next 12 months (up from 47% in July). Gold is seen as undervalued by a net 16% of managers (highest since March 2023). Jackson Hole: Fed Chair Warsh expected to strike a neutral tone, with 31% expecting a hawkish signal.

bullets.title: August seasonality flips: August options expiry removes suppressive gamma Friday
bullets.body: Jefferies warns suppressive gamma forces expire Friday with August options expiration, after which volatility is expected to change character. Since 1990, the S&P has dropped at least 7% from August to October in every midterm year except 2006. SPY volume Monday was the lowest in over a decade. CTAs are long ~$140B global equities with modestly negative flows near-term, and SPX net long positioning at a 2.4x z-score consensus per Hedgeye — setting up a SPY correction as a dip-buy opportunity, not a regime break.

bullets.title: Semiconductors under pressure: SOXX -3.5%, KOSPI -1.6%; AI pure plays down 4-7%
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector fell sharply, with SOXX down 3.5% and KOSPI off 1.6% at week open. In premarket, AI pure plays broadly declined: ALAB -5%, MRVL -6%, CRWV -4%. Optical/storage names also hit (WDC -6.7%, COHR -6.8%, LITE -6.6%) on earnings reads from Fabrinet (down 12.6%). TSMC confirmed a technological edge in backside power delivery with its A16 process ahead of Intel and Samsung, and Taiwan reported record 14.15% H1 GDP growth driven by semiconductor demand.

bullets.title: Record ETF launches in 2026 — historical pattern flags potential market top risk
bullets.body: 2026 is on pace for 1,860 ETF launches, dwarfing prior peaks: 677 IPOs in 1996 (market peaked 2000), 291 ETF launches in 2007 (market peaked Oct 2007), 458 in 2022 (peaked Jan 2022). BofA survey confirms extreme bullishness; Jefferies notes >80% of S&P 500 discretionary buybacks are now active, historically a supportive technical, but the broader sentiment/launch picture raises late-cycle concerns.

bullets.title: Manufacturing broadening beyond AI into defense, freight, infrastructure
bullets.body: July industrial production rose 0.2% m/m; tech IP jumped nearly 2% m/m with semis even stronger, and defense IP hit a cycle high. Jefferies' August Short Cycle Monitor improved for the second straight month, signaling broadening industrial recovery beyond AI into aerospace, freight, and infrastructure. Morgan Stanley confirms 54.9% of industries posted monthly gains in July, with AI-related sectors (computers, semis) continuing to support activity.

bullets.title: Housing deterioration accelerating: starts hit 3-year low, builders face sustained headwinds
bullets.body: July housing starts fell 12.4% to 1.239M SAAR (lowest single-family starts since 2022), though permits rose 5.0% to 1.443M. 22V Research maintains a bearish homebuilders call — Lennar orders -4% YoY, D.R. Horton cancellation rate rose to 20%, KB Home revenues -27% — and recommends ITB October $95 puts at ~$3. NAHB present sales and 6-month outlook both at the 17th percentile post-1985; lumber futures down 13% since July 22, signaling demand weakness.

bullets.title: FCC optical transceiver ban risk + China indium phosphide retaliation threatens data center supply chains
bullets.body: 22V Research flags the FCC moving toward banning Chinese optical transceiver imports by year-end, which Beijing frames as a Busan tech truce violation. In response, Beijing signaled retaliatory export restrictions on indium phosphide — a critical substrate for high-speed lasers used in US data center buildout. The US-China tech truce expires November 10; Xi's fall visit is a key watchpoint for extension.

bullets.title: Japanese life insurers sitting on $200B in unrealized bond losses as JGB yields surge
bullets.body: Japanese 10-year bond yields hit a three-decade peak on inflation concerns, with JGB 10Y up 25bps over the past month. Japanese life insurers are sitting on an estimated $200B in unrealized losses on bond portfolios. Jefferies noted Alts and Life Insurers are already under pressure and is moving to defensive positioning in financials.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Quad 3 call: long gold/copper dips, long software (AMZN/MSFT), short TLT/LQD
bullets.body: Hedgeye's macro regime shifted from disinflationary Quad 4 to Quad 3 on oil breaking above $83 and August CPI nowcast ticking higher. Positioning: long gold (centerpiece), buying copper dips, building AMZN and MSFT in 50-100bps tranches as both approach Risk Range lows, short TLT and LQD tactically, sold CRAK/XLE for software/quantum reallocation. Bitcoin needs to regain $68K trend; Ethereum sold after trend failure. Euro trimmed after a major run.

bullets.title: Consumer income expectations deteriorating; 56% alarmed by gas prices
bullets.body: Consumer expectations for higher income over the next year dropped to 35.1% in August, with only 8% expecting income growth to outpace inflation. Separately, 56% of Americans report being 'very concerned' about gas prices, up from 34% in January per Pew Research. Circana July retail dollars +1% YoY but units -2%, with discretionary merchandise down 4.3% in dollars and 3.9% in units.

bullets.title: Empire Manufacturing holds in expansion (ISM-adj 55) but supply chains tightening
bullets.body: The Empire Manufacturing Index adjusted to 55 in August per ISM methodology, remaining in expansion territory throughout 2024. However, the report showed significantly longer delivery times, rising backlogs, and worsening supply availability — consistent with the Quad 3 supply-constraint narrative and MLCC lead time divergence, where high-end products are approaching 10-month delays driven by AI server demand.

bullets.title: MOVE index spiked 605bps; SPX straddle at 35bps signals vol regime inflection ahead
bullets.body: The MOVE index surged 605bps, while today's SPX straddle is priced at $27.3/35bps (ref 7715), still betting on low realized volatility. VIX expiration is tomorrow. Jefferies warns suppressive gamma expires Friday with August OpEx, at which point vol is expected to change character materially.

bullets.title: Anthropic revenue run rate exceeds $65B annualized (7x YoY), nearing OpenAI
bullets.body: Anthropic is tracking to more than $65B in annualized revenue, up more than 7x from the prior year pace — and is reported to have surpassed OpenAI's annualized revenue. This catalyzed a brief rally in AI/semis and memory (+2.8%), though broader AI pure plays remained under pressure on the day from higher yields and geopolitical risk.

bullets.title: Internet sector down led by AMZN/GOOGL -4/-2%; AI ROIC debate drives valuation compression
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes internet names fell 1% (with SPX/NDX flat/+1%), led by AMZN -4% and GOOGL -2%. AMZN, GOOGL, and META trade at 20x/17x/19x 2026E EPS, down 35%/35%/19% vs. TTM average multiples. The AI ROIC debate remains front and center for sector valuation. Citi's July traffic data shows positive engagement trends: GOOGL search share at 91.3% globally, META Instagram US time spent +13% YoY to 61 mins/DAU, DASH MAUs +10% YoY, CVNA web traffic +62% YoY.

bullets.title: 30yr Treasury at 5.33% two-decade high driven by AI-IG bond issuance wave
bullets.body: AI-related IG bond issuance is crowding the market, estimated to add ~0.3ppts to the 10Y yield, with bond issuance hitting a third straight monthly record. GOOGL's $5B Kangaroo bond offering saw strong demand; BX's QTS upsized an MSFT-leased data center bond by 33% to $3.9B. The combination of massive corporate/government issuance calendars and geopolitical risk is now a global yield phenomenon with cross-border spillovers.

bullets.title: Diesel crack spread hits record high; oil above $90 signals Quad 3 consumer headwind
bullets.body: Diesel crack spreads hit an unprecedented record as refined-products markets enter what analysts describe as a crisis phase. Oil above $90 (Brent) and $83 (WTI trend break) historically precedes Q3/Q4 consumer stock declines in Hedgeye's Quad 3 framework, where inflation re-accelerates and discretionary spending tightens. Hedgeye has sold XLE/CRAK for portfolio reallocation but notes the commodity breakout is trend-confirmed.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole positioning: Warsh expected neutral; steepener trades (IVOL) favored
bullets.body: BofA's August survey shows the consensus expects Fed Chair Warsh to strike a neutral tone at Jackson Hole, though 31% expect a hawkish signal. Weak September rate cut odds fell to 30%. Multiple strategists (Hedgeye, 22V) favor yield curve steepeners (IVOL) as the most attractive fixed income trade given dovish Fed messaging alongside global inflation re-acceleration and a 10s2s spread at a new cycle high around 50-55bps.

bullets.title: Private credit stress rising: BDC non-accruals highest since 2017; July bankruptcies +11% YoY
bullets.body: Jefferies notes July bankruptcies are trending 4% higher YoY with medium-plus bankruptcies up 11% YoY. BDC non-accruals hit a median of 2.8% of portfolio cost in Q2, the highest level since 2017. C&I loan growth is running only 0.5% unannualized 3QTD vs. a 10-year trend of 0.1%. Credit card metrics at AXP, COF, SYF, and BFH remain stable to better than historical averages, providing a partial offset.
